summary: Preserve Linux process-tree custody through systemd observation admission and unit collection races

replay.detail: No graph replay or stored-state conversion is introduced; synchronous runtime custody waits for the existing fresh-observation admission boundary.

schema.detail: No persisted schema or claim contract changes are introduced by this fix.

rules.detail: No checkpoint rules or admission budget policy changes; manager observations retain their existing admission and freshness requirements.

compatibility.detail: No CLI flags, wire contracts or client capabilities change. The fixes operate within each Linux execution host and require no coordinated member upgrade.

downtime.detail: No additional interruption beyond the normal binary rollout is required; no production daemon restart was performed for the isolated proof.

manual.detail: No user state migration or manual cleanup is required by the fix. Runtime tests now own finite-tree fixture cleanup during unwinding.

recovery.detail: Synchronous teardown waits for fresh admitted observation instead of abandoning custody after invalidation. Complete not-found records from list/show collection races no longer poison unrelated observation; scope absence still requires fresh verification. PTY launcher completion and verified server migration finish scope joins so retirement can confirm the whole tree is empty.
